findingDetails.title: Retired foundations and audit identities remain in the live sk-code handoff contract
findingDetails.scopeProof: Command metadata still loads shared/sk-code-handoff.md for implementation handoff, while command-surface tests validate only the public three-command/four-mode surface and do not remove or historicize foundations/audit handoff cards.

claimAdjudication.claim: A live handoff contract loaded by current command metadata still assigns active handoff semantics to retired foundations/audit identities.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reread command metadata, shared handoff source, current registry, command-surface tests, and interface-command-contract tests. Tests prove public command topology but do not mark stale foundations/audit handoff cards historical.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The sections may be stale remnants rather than intended routes; severity remains P1 because they sit in the live implementation handoff schema consumed by current commands.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 only if the handoff contract marks those cards historical/non-selectable or command metadata stops loading this file for current implementation handoff.

findingDetails.title: Guided md-generator can delete and rewrite an arbitrary --design-md path outside the output policy
findingDetails.scopeProof: guided-run.test.ts verifies unsafe --output handling and absolute argument threading, but no negative --design-md policy case exists before the delete/write retry path.

claimAdjudication.claim: The md-generator guided runner can mutate a DESIGN.md path that was not checked by the shared output policy.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reread guided-run.ts, guided-run.test.ts, guided-run.md, and output-policy tests. The reference says the wrapper checks existing tokens/DESIGN.md paths, but implementation and tests still policy-check only output.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The mutation is local and user-selected, keeping it below P0. It remains a P1 boundary defect because a declared mutating pipeline allowlist protects output but not the second file it deletes and rewrites.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if --design-md receives an equivalent output-policy/confirmation contract or is documented as intentionally outside the declared policy boundary.

findingDetails.title: Active security NFR still requires retired audit shell/path gates to remain intact
findingDetails.scopeProof: The active NFR, accepted ADR, and checklist evidence still disagree on whether the audit security gate is live, superseded, or waived.

claimAdjudication.claim: The packet has an active security requirement to preserve audit shell/path gates even though ADR-002 retired audit and the checklist marks that gate N/A.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reread the active NFR, ADR-002 decision text, checklist security rows, implementation-summary current-stage notes, and current command topology. The topology confirms retirement but does not supersede the active NFR line.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The NFR is likely stale ADR-001 prose. It remains P1 because it is still in the active security requirements section and contradicts release checklist semantics.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if NFR-S01 is explicitly marked superseded or rewritten to the ADR-002 security rationale.

findingDetails.title: Retained foundations procedure cards are absent from the live interface selection contract
findingDetails.scopeProof: Exact searches across design-interface/SKILL.md, command-metadata.json, /interface:design, and command-surface tests found no live selection-contract references to the three retained foundations procedure-card filenames; procedure-card-schema-check.mjs reports only those three cards failing.

claimAdjudication.claim: Retained foundations procedure cards are present and release-relevant, but the live interface mode and command choreography omit them from the selectable procedure-card contract.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Reread interface routing, command choreography, /interface:design task lanes, hub foundations aliases, command tests, and reran procedure-card-schema-check.mjs. The visual-system lane and aliases preserve static-system routing, but the three retained cards remain non-selectable by filename and fail the current card schema.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The files could be intended as historical/manual-only material. That does not fit their location under design-interface/procedures plus current visual-system routing semantics, so P1 remains supported.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if maintainers mark these files non-selectable/historical or add an explicit selection mapping that intentionally bypasses procedure-card filename selection.
